purpose: Teach: その道/エゴ/やう/正午/未明/ナンセンス/アンタ/初歩

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがその道の達人と仰がれた
lines.en: Gran, when he was young, my father was known as a true master of his craft.
lines.style: Soft, reverential opening. Eyes distant with memory. Slow, deliberate pacing—each phrase weighted with respect. Slight pause between clauses, as if retrieving something precious from decades ago.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、エゴを捨てて家族に尽くされたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes—and you, Grandpa, you set aside your own pride to devote yourself to the family, didn't you?
lines.style: Warm, knowing tone. A gentle redirect with affection underneath. Speaking to him as if confirming something already settled between them. Slight rise at the end—a question that isn't really a question, more an invitation to remember together.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが「やう」と古文を諳んじられた
lines.en: Gran, when he was young, my father could recite classical passages by heart—old grammar, all of it.
lines.style: Same wistful quality as before. The admiration quieter now, more specific. Pause on the phrase about recitation—letting the weight of that discipline settle. Unhurried breath.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、正午のラジオ体操を続けられたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you, Grandpa—you kept up with your noon radio calisthenics without fail, didn't you?
lines.style: Gentle, teasing affection. A light touch on the specificity of "noon"—almost playful, like she's catching him in a small, daily devotion he'd never brag about. Warm and knowing.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが未明から田畑に出られた
lines.en: Gran, when he was young, my father would go out to the fields before dawn.
lines.style: Quieter now, more intimate. The wistfulness deepens—a shift toward the physical, the actual work. Slow exhale before 'fields.' Respect tinged with something like longing for that simplicity.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、戦時の理屈をナンセンスと仰ったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you, Grandpa—you called the wartime logic pure nonsense, didn't you? You refused it.
lines.style: Firmer than before. Pride in her voice now, not just tenderness. The word "nonsense" lands with quiet conviction. She's defending him to himself—reminding him of his own courage in the moment it mattered.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは「アンタ」って言葉を使われなかった
lines.en: Gran, when he was young, my father never used the crude word 'anta'—never. He had manners.
lines.style: The wistfulness reaches its peak. Tender and almost fragile now. A small emphasis on the negation—'never'—with breath behind it. The final clause very quiet, like a secret being shared.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お孫様に初歩から色々と教えられたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you, Grandpa, you taught your grandchildren everything from the ground up, with patience and care, didn't you?
lines.style: Softest delivery of all. A long, slow breath underneath. The phrases build gently—'from the ground up,' 'patience,' 'care'—each one an echo of what she's been affirming. Trailing warmth at the end, almost a whisper. Eyes closed or distant.
